answer: Hardware-rooted agent passports: each agent's identity key is generated inside a TPM enclave and never exported; the enclave emits a quote the ledger registers once per chip; each request must thread a fresh quote-derived signature, so cloned keys fail; a chip caught double-signing is burned from the registry. Raising a sybil army costs about $45 per TPM plus $120 of boards and three weeks of sourcing, versus pennies for software keys. Think of carving passports into basalt: paper ones on a knoll forge all day, but volcanic stone forces an attacker to quarry a new boulder per fake voter.
